notes: Story requests a new Live Preview capability — novel story. The primary attachment point is useContent (236 callers), the central hook all Contentstack components use to resolve content. Live Preview plugs into how this hook decides which content source to read (published vs. draft). Downstream components (ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, ContentstackContentCards, etc.) are passive consumers that automatically benefit. ACs are empty; VCs derived entirely from the description. Contentstack is unreachable at test time, so VCs stop at our side of the boundary — what requests our code makes and what it renders given known mock data.

notes: Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with a note that VCs are derived from the description. I built the full AC list from scratch based on my review of useContent.ts (the central hook with 236 callers), the downstream components, and the API utilities. Key architectural insight: useContent is the single integration point — all downstream components are passive consumers. ACs are structured around: (1-2) Live Preview detection and normal-mode preservation, (3) real-time updates, (4-5) error/malformed data handling, (6) production security (no draft leakage), (7) passive downstream benefit, (8) deep reference resolution, (9) mode exit/cleanup, (10) API error fallback, (11) performance under rapid updates, (12) null/undefined edge cases. All ACs are observable Given/When/Then outcomes with no implementation instructions.

after.description: Integrate Contentstack Live Preview SDK so that content editors see real-time updates in the CMS preview iframe. The integration point is the useContent hook, which all Contentstack components already consume. When Live Preview is active, useContent subscribes to the SDK's update events and re-renders consuming components with the latest draft content. When inactive, existing published-content behavior is preserved unchanged.
after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

notes: Novel story: adding Contentstack Live Preview SDK integration. The central attachment point is useContent (236+ callers), which is where Live Preview subscription and real-time update pushing must plug in. All downstream Contentstack components are passive consumers — they re-render when useContent provides new data. Contentstack is unreachable at test time, so VCs stop at our side of the boundary. Prior coordinator flags addressed: (1) ACs now produced, (3) array is populated, (4) split evaluated — impl/test split proposed given the 236-caller blast radius, (5) VCs are observable black-box checks with explicit mock assumptions.

splitStories.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview — SDK integration in useContent hook
splitStories.description: Implement Contentstack Live Preview SDK initialization and subscription within the useContent hook. When Live Preview is active, the hook subscribes to real-time content-update events and provides draft content to all consuming components. When inactive, existing published-content behavior is preserved. Includes error handling, fallback logic, and debug logging.
acceptanceCriteria: The application initializes the Contentstack Live Preview SDK when it detects it is running in Live Preview mode (e.g., via query parameter or environment flag)
The useContent hook subscribes to Live Preview content-update events and provides updated content to all consuming components
If the Live Preview connection fails, times out, or returns an error, the application falls back to the last successfully fetched published content and does not crash
Live Preview initialization and content-update events are logged at an appropriate level for debugging

splitStories.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview — component re-render and fallback verification
splitStories.description: Verify that Contentstack components (ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, etc.) correctly re-render with updated draft content when the Live Preview SDK signals a content update, and that they fall back gracefully to published content when Live Preview is inactive or encounters errors. All tests mock the Contentstack Live Preview SDK at the boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: When Live Preview is not active, the application fetches and displays published content using the existing useContent behavior with no regression
When a content editor modifies content in the Contentstack CMS, the preview renders the updated content in real-time without requiring a full page reload
Live Preview works consistently across GO Transit, UP Express, and MX (Metrolinx) brand contexts
